11	/-!
12	# The Albanese universal property of `Pic⁰_{C/k}`
13	
14	This file states Milne's
15	*Abelian Varieties* §III.6 Proposition 6.1: for a complete nonsingular curve
16	`C` of genus `g > 0` over an algebraically closed field `k̄` and a marked
17	`k̄`-point `P₀ ∈ C(k̄)`, the Abel–Jacobi morphism
18	`ι_{P₀} : C ⟶ Pic⁰_{C/k̄}` is the **Albanese morphism** of the pointed curve
19	`(C, P₀)`: any pointed morphism `φ : C ⟶ A` into an abelian variety with
20	`φ(P₀) = η_A` factors uniquely as `φ = ψ ∘ ι_{P₀}` for a homomorphism of
21	group schemes `ψ : Pic⁰_{C/k̄} ⟶ A`.
22	
23	The route taken is the **symmetric-power route** (cube-free): the
24	symmetric assignment `(P₁,…,P_g) ↦ φ(P₁) + ⋯ + φ(P_g)` factors through
25	`Sym^g C`, the resulting morphism `Sym^g φ : Sym^g C ⟶ A` descends through
26	the birational morphism `f^{(g)} : Sym^g C ⟶ Pic⁰_{C/k̄}` to a rational map
27	`Pic⁰_{C/k̄} ⇢ A`, and Milne's Theorem I.3.2 (`extend_to_av` in the sibling
28	`Albanese/Thm32RationalMapExtension.lean`, A.4.c) promotes it to a regular
29	morphism `ψ : Pic⁰_{C/k̄} ⟶ A`. The group-homomorphism property of `ψ` then
30	follows from `ψ(η_J) = η_A` together with Milne Corollary I.1.2 (a
31	consequence of `thm:rigidity_lemma`).
32	
33	## Main results
34	
35	* `Pic0.abelJacobi` — the regular morphism `ι_{P₀} : C ⟶ Pic⁰_{C/k̄}`
36	  (`lem:abel_jacobi_morphism`).
37	* `Pic0.SymmetricPower` — the `g`-th symmetric power `Sym^g C` of the curve
38	  `C`, as a `k̄`-scheme (Milne III.3 Proposition 3.1).
39	* `Pic0.symmetricPowerAVMap` — the symmetrised morphism
40	  `Sym^g φ : Sym^g C ⟶ A` induced by a morphism `φ : C ⟶ A` into an abelian
41	  variety.
42	* `Pic0.symmetricPowerToJacobian` — the birational morphism
43	  `f^{(g)} : Sym^g C ⟶ Pic⁰_{C/k̄}`.
44	* `Pic0.descentThroughBirationalSigma` — the descent of `Sym^g φ` to a unique
45	  regular morphism `ψ : Pic⁰_{C/k̄} ⟶ A`, via Milne Theorem I.3.2.
46	* `Pic0.albanese_eq_iff_symmetricPower_eq` — the connecting biconditional:
47	  `φ = ι_{P₀} ≫ ψ` holds iff `Sym^g φ = f^{(g)} ≫ ψ`.
48	* `Pic0.albanese_universal_property` — the universal property itself (Milne
49	  Proposition III.6.1), assembled from the previous two.
50	
51	## Remaining obligations
52	
53	`albanese_universal_property` is assembled from
54	`descentThroughBirationalSigma` and `albanese_eq_iff_symmetricPower_eq`, but
55	six declarations of this file are stated without proof:
56	
57	* `abelJacobi` — the moduli classifier of the rigidified diagonal
58	  correspondence `𝓛^{P₀} = 𝓞_{C × C}(Δ − {P₀} × C − C × {P₀})`, taken as a
59	  relative degree-zero line bundle over the second factor.
60	* `SymmetricPower` — the affine-and-glue construction `Spec(A^{⊗ g})^{S_g}`
61	  of Milne III.3 Proposition 3.1 (Mumford 1970 §II.7 / §III.11). Mathlib has
62	  no scheme-theoretic symmetric power, only `Sym` for types and modules.
63	* `symmetricPowerAVMap` and `symmetricPowerToJacobian` — the two invocations
64	  of the universal property of `Sym^g C`, which need the symmetric projection
65	  `π : C^g ⟶ Sym^g C` supplied by that construction.
66	* `descentThroughBirationalSigma` — extension of the rational map
67	  `Sym^g φ ∘ (f^{(g)})^{-1}` to a regular morphism (Milne Theorem I.3.2).
68	* `albanese_eq_iff_symmetricPower_eq` — Milne's identification of `ι_{P₀}`
69	  with `Q ↦ Q + (g − 1) P₀` followed by `f^{(g)}`.
70	
71	## The scheme `Pic⁰_{C/k̄}`
72	
73	`Pic⁰_{C/k̄}` is taken from `Picard/Pic0AbelianVariety.lean` through a thin
74	`Pic0.Bundle` structure that carries the underlying scheme together with its
75	four abelian-variety attributes (`GrpObj`, `IsProper`, `Smooth`,
76	`GeometricallyIrreducible`), the carrier `Pic0.bundle C`, and the derived
77	definition `Pic0.jacobianScheme C := (bundle C).scheme`.
78	
79	The upstream declarations `Scheme.Pic0.{grpObj, proper, smooth,
80	geometricallyIrreducible}` run under `[GeometricallyIntegral C.hom]`,
81	`[HasPicScheme C]` and `[PicScheme.PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType C]`, whereas
82	the Albanese curve enters carrying only smoothness, properness and geometric
83	irreducibility over `k̄`. The three bridges of §0.0
84	(`geometricallyReduced_of_smooth`, `GeometricallyIntegral.of_…`,
85	`hasRationalPoint_of_isAlgClosed`) discharge the missing hypotheses over an
86	algebraically closed base.
87	
88	## Abelian-variety conventions
89	
90	Following the project (cf. `AbelianVarietyRigidity.lean`, `Jacobian.lean`),
91	an **abelian variety over `k̄`** is encoded as an object
92	`A : Over (Spec (.of k̄))` carrying the four instances:
93	
94	- `[GrpObj A]` (group-object structure on the over-category),
95	- `[IsProper A.hom]` (complete),
96	- `[Smooth A.hom]` (nonsingular),
97	- `[GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom]` (geometrically irreducible).
98	
99	A **smooth proper geometrically irreducible curve over `k̄`** carries:
100	
101	- `[SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]`,
102	- `[IsProper C.hom]`,
103	- `[GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]`.
104	
105	These instances are supplied by `inferInstance` at the call site.
106	
107	## References
108	
109	Blueprint: `blueprint/src/chapters/Albanese_AlbaneseUP.tex`.
110	Milne, *Abelian Varieties*, §III.6 Proposition 6.1, p. 104;
111	§III.3 Proposition 3.1 (symmetric power), p. 94; §III.5 Theorem 5.1(a)
112	(birationality of `f^{(g)}`), p. 101 (`references/abelian-varieties.pdf`).
113	-/

123	/-! ## §0.0. Substrate bridges: geometric integrality and rational points
124	
125	`Picard/Pic0AbelianVariety.lean` states `Pic⁰_{C/k}` smooth,
126	proper and geometrically irreducible under the hypotheses
127	`[GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicScheme C]
128	[PicScheme.PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType C]`, whereas the Albanese curve `C`
129	enters here carrying only `[SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
130	[GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]` over an algebraically closed field `k̄`. The
131	three bridging facts below discharge the missing hypotheses, so that
132	`Pic0.bundle` can be assembled from the upstream declarations. -/
133	
134	/-- **Reducedness descends along a faithfully flat morphism.** If `π : Y ⟶ X` is
135	flat and surjective (i.e. faithfully flat) and `Y` is reduced, then `X` is
136	reduced: each stalk map `𝒪_{X,π(y)} → 𝒪_{Y,y}` is a flat local homomorphism of
137	local rings, hence faithfully flat and in particular injective, so `𝒪_{X,π(y)}`
138	embeds into the reduced ring `𝒪_{Y,y}`. -/
139	theorem isReduced_of_flat_of_surjective {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (π : Y ⟶ X)
140	    [Flat π] [Surjective π] [IsReduced Y] : IsReduced X := by
141	  haveI hst : ∀ x : X, _root_.IsReduced (X.presheaf.stalk x) := by
142	    intro x
143	    obtain ⟨y, rfl⟩ := π.surjective x
144	    have hlocal : IsLocalHom (π.stalkMap y).hom := inferInstance
145	    have hflat : (π.stalkMap y).hom.Flat := Flat.stalkMap π y
146	    have hinj : Function.Injective (π.stalkMap y).hom := by
147	      algebraize [(π.stalkMap y).hom]
148	      haveI : Module.Flat (X.presheaf.stalk (π.base y)) (Y.presheaf.stalk y) := hflat
149	      haveI : IsLocalHom (algebraMap (X.presheaf.stalk (π.base y)) (Y.presheaf.stalk y)) := hlocal
150	      haveI : Module.FaithfullyFlat (X.presheaf.stalk (π.base y)) (Y.presheaf.stalk y) :=
151	        Module.FaithfullyFlat.of_flat_of_isLocalHom
152	      exact FaithfulSMul.algebraMap_injective _ _
153	    exact isReduced_of_injective (π.stalkMap y).hom hinj
154	  exact isReduced_of_isReduced_stalk X
155	
156	/-- **A scheme smooth over an algebraically closed field is geometrically
157	reduced.** For each test field `K/k̄`, the base change `X ×_{k̄} K` is smooth
158	over `K`; its further base change to `K̄ = AlgebraicClosure K` is smooth over an
159	algebraically closed field, hence reduced
160	(`Scheme.isReduced_of_smooth_of_isAlgClosed`), and reducedness descends along the
161	faithfully flat projection `X_{K̄} → X_K` (`isReduced_of_flat_of_surjective`). -/
162	theorem geometricallyReduced_of_smooth {kbar : Type u} [Field kbar] [IsAlgClosed kbar]
163	    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of kbar)) [Smooth f] :
164	    GeometricallyReduced f := by
165	  refine ⟨?_⟩
166	  rw [geometrically_iff_of_commRing_of_isClosedUnderIsomorphisms]
167	  intro K _ _
168	  have hfsurj : (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K (AlgebraicClosure K))).hom.FaithfullyFlat :=
169	    RingHom.faithfullyFlat_algebraMap_iff.mpr inferInstance
170	  have hFS := (flat_and_surjective_SpecMap_iff
171	    (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K (AlgebraicClosure K)))).mpr hfsurj
172	  haveI : Flat (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K (AlgebraicClosure K)))) := hFS.1
173	  haveI : Surjective (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K (AlgebraicClosure K)))) := hFS.2
174	  haveI hsm1 : Smooth (pullback.snd f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap kbar K)))) :=
175	    inferInstance
176	  haveI hsm2 : Smooth (pullback.snd
177	      (pullback.snd f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap kbar K))))
178	      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K (AlgebraicClosure K))))) := inferInstance
179	  haveI : Smooth (Over.mk (pullback.snd
180	      (pullback.snd f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap kbar K))))
181	      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K (AlgebraicClosure K)))))).hom := hsm2
182	  haveI : IsReduced (pullback (pullback.snd f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap kbar K))))
183	      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K (AlgebraicClosure K))))) :=
184	    Scheme.isReduced_of_smooth_of_isAlgClosed (kbar := AlgebraicClosure K) (Over.mk (pullback.snd
185	      (pullback.snd f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap kbar K))))
186	      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K (AlgebraicClosure K))))))
187	  exact isReduced_of_flat_of_surjective
188	    (pullback.fst (pullback.snd f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap kbar K))))
189	      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K (AlgebraicClosure K)))))
190	
191	/-- **A smooth, geometrically irreducible curve over an algebraically closed
192	field has a rational point.** `C.left` is nonempty (geometric irreducibility over
193	the one-point base `Spec k̄`), locally of finite type over `k̄` (smoothness) and
194	therefore a Jacobson space, so it has a closed point `x`; over the algebraically
195	closed field `k̄`, `pointOfClosedPoint`/`pointEquivClosedPoint` promote `x` to a
196	`k̄`-rational section of `C.hom`. This discharges `[HasRationalPoint C]`. -/
197	theorem hasRationalPoint_of_isAlgClosed {kbar : Type u} [Field kbar] [IsAlgClosed kbar]
198	    (C : Over (Spec (.of kbar))) [Smooth C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
199	    Scheme.HasRationalPoint C := by
200	  haveI : LocallyOfFiniteType C.hom := inferInstance
201	  haveI : IrreducibleSpace C.left :=
202	    GeometricallyIrreducible.irreducibleSpace_of_subsingleton C.hom
203	  haveI : JacobsonSpace C.left := LocallyOfFiniteType.jacobsonSpace C.hom
204	  obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := nonempty_inter_closedPoints (X := C.left) (Z := Set.univ)
205	    Set.univ_nonempty isClosed_univ.isLocallyClosed
206	  exact ⟨⟨(pointEquivClosedPoint C.hom).symm ⟨x, hx.2⟩⟩⟩
207	
208	namespace Pic0
209	
210	/-! ## §0. File-internal placeholder for `Pic⁰_{C/k̄}`
211	
212	The identity component of the Picard scheme, together with its degree map, is
213	constructed in `Picard/Pic0AbelianVariety.lean`. The helper below — a bundled
214	structure carrying the Pic⁰ scheme together with its four abelian-variety
215	instances, plus the carrier `bundle` — supplies the interface. `bundle` is
216	wired to the upstream declarations (`Scheme.Pic0Scheme`,
217	`Scheme.Pic0.{grpObj, proper, smooth, geometricallyIrreducible}`) through the
218	§0.0 bridges; the derived `jacobianScheme` def and the four typeclass carriers
219	below are projections from `bundle`. -/
220	
221	/-- Interface for `Pic⁰_{C/k̄}`: bundles the underlying `k̄`-scheme together
222	with the four abelian-variety structural instances (group object, proper,
223	smooth, geometrically irreducible). -/
224	structure Bundle {kbar : Type u} [Field kbar] [IsAlgClosed kbar]
225	    (C : Over (Spec (.of kbar)))
226	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
227	    [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] where
228	  /-- The underlying scheme `Pic⁰_{C/k̄}`. -/
229	  scheme : Over (Spec (.of kbar))
230	  /-- Group-object structure on `Pic⁰_{C/k̄}`. -/
231	  grpObj : GrpObj scheme
232	  /-- Properness of `Pic⁰_{C/k̄}` over `k̄`. -/
233	  proper : IsProper scheme.hom
234	  /-- Smoothness of `Pic⁰_{C/k̄}` over `k̄`. -/
235	  smooth : Smooth scheme.hom
236	  /-- Geometric irreducibility of `Pic⁰_{C/k̄}` over `k̄`. -/
237	  geomIrred : GeometricallyIrreducible scheme.hom
238	
239	variable {kbar : Type u} [Field kbar] [IsAlgClosed kbar]
240	
241	variable (C : Over (Spec (.of kbar)))
242	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
243	    [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
244	
245	/-- **The `Pic⁰_{C/k̄}` bundle.** For a smooth
246	proper geometrically irreducible curve `C` over an algebraically closed field
247	`k̄`, the underlying scheme is `Scheme.Pic0Scheme C` and its four
248	abelian-variety attributes are the identity-component theorems of
249	`Picard/Pic0AbelianVariety.lean` (`Scheme.Pic0.{grpObj, proper, smooth,
250	geometricallyIrreducible}`).
251	
252	The upstream declarations run under `[GeometricallyIntegral C.hom]`,
253	`[HasPicScheme C]` and `[PicScheme.PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType C]`; over `k̄`
254	these are discharged honestly here:
255	`geometricallyReduced_of_smooth` + `GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom` give
256	`GeometricallyIntegral C.hom`; `hasRationalPoint_of_isAlgClosed` gives
257	`[HasRationalPoint C]`, whence `instHasPicScheme` supplies `[HasPicScheme C]` and
258	`instPicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType` the local-finiteness carrier. -/
259	noncomputable def bundle : Bundle C := by
260	  haveI : Smooth C.hom := SmoothOfRelativeDimension.smooth 1 C.hom
261	  haveI : GeometricallyReduced C.hom := geometricallyReduced_of_smooth C.hom
262	  haveI : GeometricallyIntegral C.hom :=
263	    GeometricallyIntegral.of_geometricallyReduced_of_geometricallyIrreducible C.hom
264	  haveI : Scheme.HasRationalPoint C := hasRationalPoint_of_isAlgClosed C
265	  exact
266	    { scheme := Scheme.Pic0Scheme C
267	      grpObj := (Scheme.Pic0.grpObj C).some
268	      proper := Scheme.Pic0.proper C
269	      smooth := Scheme.Pic0.smooth C
270	      geomIrred := Scheme.Pic0.geometricallyIrreducible C }
271	
272	/-- The underlying `k̄`-scheme `Pic⁰_{C/k̄}` of a smooth proper
273	geometrically irreducible curve `C` over an algebraically closed field
274	`k̄`. Read off from the `Bundle` interface. -/
275	noncomputable def jacobianScheme : Over (Spec (.of kbar)) := (bundle C).scheme
276	
277	/-- Group-object structure on `Pic⁰_{C/k̄}`. Deliberately **not** an
278	`instance`: while `Pic⁰_{C/k̄}` still depends on unproved upstream
279	statements, making this an instance would let `sorryAx` propagate silently
280	through typeclass synthesis. Consumers thread it explicitly via
281	`letI := jacobianScheme_grpObj C`. -/
282	@[implicit_reducible]
283	noncomputable def jacobianScheme_grpObj : GrpObj (jacobianScheme C) :=
284	  (bundle C).grpObj
285	
286	/-- (Deliberately not an `instance`; see `jacobianScheme_grpObj`.) -/
287	theorem jacobianScheme_isProper : IsProper (jacobianScheme C).hom :=
288	  (bundle C).proper
289	
290	/-- (Deliberately not an `instance`; see `jacobianScheme_grpObj`.) -/
291	theorem jacobianScheme_smooth : Smooth (jacobianScheme C).hom :=
292	  (bundle C).smooth
293	
294	/-- (Deliberately not an `instance`; see `jacobianScheme_grpObj`.) -/
295	theorem jacobianScheme_geomIrred :
296	    GeometricallyIrreducible (jacobianScheme C).hom :=
297	  (bundle C).geomIrred
298	
299	/-! ## §1. The Abel–Jacobi morphism at a marked point
300	
301	The first sub-lemma packages the construction and elementary regularity
302	of the Abel–Jacobi morphism `ι_{P₀} : C ⟶ Pic⁰_{C/k̄}` at the basepoint
303	`P₀ ∈ C(k̄)`. On `k̄`-points,
304	`ι_{P₀}(Q) = [𝓞_C(Q − P₀)] ∈ Pic⁰_{C/k̄}(k̄)`; at the basepoint
305	itself `ι_{P₀}(P₀) = η_J`.
306	
307	The morphism is the moduli classifier of
308	the rigidified diagonal correspondence
309	`𝓛^{P₀} = 𝓞_{C × C}(Δ − {P₀} × C − C × {P₀})` on `C × C`, taken as a
310	relative degree-zero line bundle on `C × C` over the second factor.
311	
312	Blueprint reference: `lem:abel_jacobi_morphism` (Milne, *Abelian
313	Varieties*, Proposition III.6.1 and Summary III.6.11). -/
314	
315	/-- **The Abel–Jacobi morphism at the marked basepoint `P₀`.**
316	
317	For a smooth proper geometrically irreducible curve `C` over an
318	algebraically closed field `k̄` and a marked `k̄`-point
319	`P₀ : 𝟙_ ⟶ C`, the **Abel–Jacobi morphism** is the unique regular
320	morphism `ι_{P₀} : C ⟶ Pic⁰_{C/k̄}` characterised on `T`-points by the
321	formula `(1 × ι_{P₀})^* 𝓜^{P₀} ≈ 𝓛^{P₀}`, where `𝓜^{P₀}` is the
322	Poincaré–Picard correspondence on `C × Pic⁰_{C/k̄}` and
323	`𝓛^{P₀} = 𝓞_{C × C}(Δ − {P₀} × C − C × {P₀})`.
324	
325	**Not yet constructed.** The construction applies the moduli interpretation
326	of `Pic⁰_{C/k̄}` (`def:pic_scheme` together with its identity-component
327	refinement) to the relative degree-zero line bundle `𝓛^{P₀}` on
328	`C × C → C` along the second projection; Yoneda then produces the
329	unique classifying morphism `C ⟶ Pic⁰_{C/k̄}`. The basepoint
330	condition `P₀ ≫ abelJacobi C P₀ = η[Pic⁰_{C/k̄}]` (`lem:abel_jacobi_morphism`)
331	holds because the restriction of `𝓛^{P₀}` to `C × {P₀}` is the trivial
332	line bundle `𝓞_C(P₀ − P₀) ≅ 𝓞_C`, whose moduli class is `η_J`. -/
333	noncomputable def abelJacobi (P0 : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of kbar))) ⟶ C) :
334	    C ⟶ jacobianScheme C :=
335	  sorry
336	
337	/-! ## §2. The `g`-th symmetric power `Sym^g C`
338	
339	The `g`-th symmetric power of `C` is the quotient of the `g`-fold
340	Cartesian power `C^g` by the natural permutation action of the
341	symmetric group `S_g`. Mathlib `b80f227` has no formalised symmetric
342	power of a scheme — only `Sym` / `SymmetricPower` for types and
343	modules — so the scheme-theoretic construction must be supplied
344	project-side, following Milne's recipe of §III.3 Proposition 3.1: on
345	each open affine `U = Spec A ⊆ C` form `Spec(A^{⊗ g})^{S_g}`, then glue
346	along the standard open-cover patching (Mumford 1970 §II.7 / §III.11).
347	
348	The construction is a prerequisite for the bodies of
349	`symmetricPowerAVMap` and `symmetricPowerToJacobian`, which need the
350	symmetric projection `π : C^g ⟶ Sym^g C` and its universal property. The
351	declaration below records the target `Sym^g C : Over (Spec k̄)` only; the
352	affine-and-glue construction is not yet formalised.
353	
354	Blueprint reference: `def:symmetric_power_curve` (Milne, *Abelian
355	Varieties*, §III.3, Proposition 3.1, p. 94). -/
356	
357	/-- **The `g`-th symmetric power `Sym^g C`** of a complete nonsingular
358	curve `C` over an algebraically closed field `k̄`, as a `k̄`-scheme.
359	
360	Milne III.3 Proposition 3.1 constructs `Sym^g C` as the quotient of
361	`C^g` by the natural permutation action of the symmetric group `S_g`:
362	on each open affine `U = Spec A ⊆ C`, form `Spec(A^{⊗ g})^{S_g}`, then
363	glue along the standard open-cover patching. The construction comes
364	equipped with a canonical finite surjective symmetric morphism
365	`π : C^g ⟶ Sym^g C` characterised by the universal property that
366	every `S_g`-symmetric morphism `C^g ⟶ T` factors uniquely through `π`.
367	
368	This declaration records the target scheme `Sym^g C`; the projection `π` and
369	its universal property belong with the construction.
370	
371	**Not yet constructed.** The body is the gluing-of-affines
372	`Spec(A^{⊗ g})^{S_g}` construction over an open affine cover of `C`.
373	
374	The signature mentions `C` explicitly (not via the file's `variable`
375	block) so that the declaration's first explicit argument is the curve
376	`C`, matching the call sites `SymmetricPower C g`. -/
377	noncomputable def SymmetricPower
378	    (C : Over (Spec (.of kbar)))
379	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
380	    [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
381	    (_g : ℕ) : Over (Spec (.of kbar)) :=
382	  sorry
383	
384	/-! ## §3. The morphism `Sym^g φ : Sym^g C ⟶ A`
385	
386	The second sub-lemma is the elementary fact that the symmetric
387	assignment `(P₁,…,P_g) ↦ φ(P₁) + ⋯ + φ(P_g)` from `C^g` to `A`
388	descends through `π : C^g ⟶ Sym^g C`. The key point is that the
389	`g`-fold addition morphism `add_A : A^g ⟶ A` is itself `S_g`-symmetric
390	because the underlying group object `A` is commutative as a group
391	scheme; combined with the universal property of `Sym^g C`, this yields
392	the unique factorisation.
393	
394	Blueprint reference: `lem:symmetric_product_av_map` (Milne's proof of
395	III.6.1, p. 104, "Clearly this is symmetric, and so it factors through
396	`C^{(g)}`"). -/
397	
398	/-- **The symmetrised morphism `Sym^g φ : Sym^g C ⟶ A`.**
399	
400	Let `φ : C ⟶ A` be a morphism into an abelian variety `A` over `k̄`.
401	The composition `add_A ∘ φ^{×g} : C^g ⟶ A^g ⟶ A` sending
402	`(P₁,…,P_g) ↦ φ(P₁) + ⋯ + φ(P_g)` is `S_g`-equivariant (where `S_g`
403	permutes the factors of `C^g` and acts trivially on `A`), because
404	addition in a commutative group object is order-independent. By the
405	universal property of `Sym^g C` (`def:symmetric_power_curve`) it
406	factors uniquely as `Sym^g φ ∘ π = add_A ∘ φ^{×g}`.
407	
408	**Not yet constructed.** The body is the universal-property invocation on
409	the symmetric composition `add_A ∘ φ^{×g}`, which needs the projection `π`
410	and its universal property from the construction of `Sym^g C`. -/
411	noncomputable def symmetricPowerAVMap (g : ℕ)
412	    {A : Over (Spec (.of kbar))}
413	    [GrpObj A] [IsProper A.hom] [Smooth A.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom]
414	    (_φ : C ⟶ A) :
415	    SymmetricPower C g ⟶ A :=
416	  sorry
417	
418	/-! ## §4. The birational morphism `Sym^g C ⟶ Pic⁰_{C/k̄}`
419	
420	The third sub-lemma is the birational identification of `Sym^g C` with
421	`Pic⁰_{C/k̄}`. After choosing the basepoint `P₀ ∈ C(k̄)`, the cycle
422	map `(P₁,…,P_g) ↦ [𝓞_C(P₁ + ⋯ + P_g − g P₀)]` defines a regular
423	morphism `f^{(g)} : Sym^g C ⟶ Pic⁰_{C/k̄}` which is birational by
424	Milne III Theorem 5.1(a) (the proof uses dimension count plus the
425	Riemann–Roch identification of the generic fibre as a single point on
426	a curve of genus `g`).
427	
428	Blueprint reference: `lem:symmetric_product_to_jacobian` (Milne,
429	*Abelian Varieties*, Theorem III.5.1(a), p. 101). -/
430	
431	/-- **The birational morphism `f^{(g)} : Sym^g C ⟶ Pic⁰_{C/k̄}`.**
432	
433	Given a basepoint `P₀ : 𝟙_ ⟶ C`, the symmetrisation of the Abel–Jacobi
434	morphism `add_J ∘ ι_{P₀}^{×g} : C^g ⟶ J^g ⟶ J` descends through
435	`π : C^g ⟶ Sym^g C` to a regular morphism
436	`f^{(g)} : Sym^g C ⟶ Pic⁰_{C/k̄}` sending an effective divisor class
437	`[P₁ + ⋯ + P_g]` to `[𝓞_C(P₁ + ⋯ + P_g − g P₀)] ∈ Pic⁰_{C/k̄}(k̄)`.
438	By Milne III Theorem 5.1(a) this morphism is *birational*: it is
439	dominant with one-dimensional fibres, and its generic fibre is a single
440	`k̄`-point (the linear system `|D|` of a general degree-`g` divisor `D`
441	on a curve of genus `g` is `0`-dimensional by Riemann–Roch).
442	
443	The birationality data (a dense open subset `U ⊆ Sym^g C` mapping
444	isomorphically onto a dense open `V ⊆ Pic⁰_{C/k̄}`) is what
445	`descentThroughBirationalSigma` consumes.
446	
447	**Not yet constructed.** The body is the specialisation of
448	`symmetricPowerAVMap` to `A := jacobianScheme C` and
449	`φ := abelJacobi C P₀`. -/
450	noncomputable def symmetricPowerToJacobian
451	    (_P0 : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of kbar))) ⟶ C) (g : ℕ) :
452	    SymmetricPower C g ⟶ jacobianScheme C :=
453	  sorry
454	
455	/-! ## §5. Descent through the birational quotient
456	
457	The final auxiliary lemma packages the two-step descent that promotes
458	`Sym^g φ : Sym^g C ⟶ A` (after passing through the birational morphism
459	`f^{(g)} : Sym^g C ⟶ Pic⁰_{C/k̄}`) to a regular morphism
460	`ψ : Pic⁰_{C/k̄} ⟶ A`. The descent is a rational map
461	`Pic⁰_{C/k̄} ⇢ A` on the dense open of `Pic⁰_{C/k̄}` on which
462	`f^{(g)}` is an isomorphism, then promoted to a regular morphism via
463	Milne's Theorem I.3.2 (the sibling `Albanese/Thm32RationalMapExtension.lean`).
464	This is the only step of the proof that uses the rational-map extension.
465	
466	Blueprint reference: `lem:descent_through_birational_sigma` (Milne's
467	proof of III.6.1, p. 104, "It therefore defines a rational map
468	`ψ : J → A`, which (I 3.2) shows to be a regular map"). -/
469	
470	/-- **Descent of `Sym^g φ` to a regular morphism `ψ : Pic⁰_{C/k̄} ⟶ A`.**
471	
472	There is a *unique* regular morphism `ψ : Pic⁰_{C/k̄} ⟶ A` such that
473	`symmetricPowerAVMap C (genus C) φ = symmetricPowerToJacobian C P₀ (genus C) ≫ ψ`
474	(equivalently, `ψ` is the unique regular extension of the rational map
475	`Sym^g φ ∘ (f^{(g)})^{-1} : Pic⁰_{C/k̄} ⇢ A`).
476	
477	The rational map is constructed on the dense open `V ⊆ Pic⁰_{C/k̄}`
478	where `f^{(g)}` is an isomorphism, then promoted to a regular morphism
479	on all of `Pic⁰_{C/k̄}` via Milne's Theorem I.3.2 (sibling
480	`Scheme.RationalMap.extend_to_av` in
481	`Albanese/Thm32RationalMapExtension.lean`). Uniqueness is the
482	standard reduced-and-separated agreement principle: two regular
483	morphisms `Pic⁰_{C/k̄} ⟶ A` agreeing on a dense open are equal.
484	
485	**Not yet proved.** The proof invokes `Scheme.RationalMap.extend_to_av` on
486	the rational map produced by inverting `f^{(g)}` on its dense open of
487	isomorphism. -/
488	theorem descentThroughBirationalSigma
489	    (P0 : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of kbar))) ⟶ C)
490	    {A : Over (Spec (.of kbar))}
491	    [GrpObj A] [IsProper A.hom] [Smooth A.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom]
492	    (φ : C ⟶ A) (_hφ : P0 ≫ φ = η[A]) :
493	    ∃! (ψ : jacobianScheme C ⟶ A),
494	      symmetricPowerAVMap C (genus C) φ
495	        = symmetricPowerToJacobian C P0 (genus C) ≫ ψ := by
496	  sorry
497	
498	/-! ## §5.5. Albanese ⇔ symmetric-power equation (connecting biconditional)
499	
500	This section isolates the *connecting identity* between the Albanese-form
501	factorisation `φ = abelJacobi C P₀ ≫ ψ` and the symmetric-power-form
502	factorisation `symmetricPowerAVMap C (genus C) φ =
503	symmetricPowerToJacobian C P₀ (genus C) ≫ ψ`. Given that biconditional,
504	`albanese_universal_property` follows from
505	`descentThroughBirationalSigma` by pure assembly. -/
506	
507	/-- **Connecting biconditional: Albanese-form equation ⇔ symmetric-power-form
508	equation.**
509	
510	For every candidate descent morphism `ψ : Pic⁰_{C/k̄} ⟶ A`, the Albanese-form
511	factorisation `φ = abelJacobi C P₀ ≫ ψ` holds iff the symmetric-power-form
512	factorisation `symmetricPowerAVMap C (genus C) φ = symmetricPowerToJacobian
513	C P₀ (genus C) ≫ ψ` holds. The forward direction precomposes both sides of
514	the Albanese equation with the symmetric `g`-fold sum, then descends through
515	`π : C^g ⟶ Sym^g C` and uses the additivity of `ψ` (a homomorphism of group
516	schemes). The reverse direction restricts the symmetric-power-form equation
517	along the diagonal embedding `Q ↦ (Q, P₀, …, P₀)` and uses
518	`φ(P₀) = η_A`.
519	
520	**Not yet proved.** The proof uses the `Sym^g` projection `π` and its
521	universal property, together with the Milne III §6 identification of
522	`ι_{P₀}` with the composite of `Q ↦ Q + (g − 1) P₀` followed by
523	`f^{(g)}`. -/
524	theorem albanese_eq_iff_symmetricPower_eq
525	    (P0 : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of kbar))) ⟶ C)
526	    {A : Over (Spec (.of kbar))}
527	    [GrpObj A] [IsProper A.hom] [Smooth A.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom]
528	    (φ : C ⟶ A) (_hφ : P0 ≫ φ = η[A]) :
529	    ∀ (ψ : jacobianScheme C ⟶ A),
530	      (φ = abelJacobi C P0 ≫ ψ) ↔
531	      (symmetricPowerAVMap C (genus C) φ
532	        = symmetricPowerToJacobian C P0 (genus C) ≫ ψ) :=
533	  sorry
534	
535	/-! ## §6. The Albanese universal property — headline theorem
536	
537	The headline result of the chapter: for every pointed morphism
538	`φ : C ⟶ A` into an abelian variety `A` with `φ(P₀) = η_A`, there
539	exists a unique regular morphism `ψ : Pic⁰_{C/k̄} ⟶ A` such that
540	`φ = ψ ∘ ι_{P₀}`. The proof follows Milne Proposition III.6.1
541	verbatim, using the four sub-lemmas above plus Milne Theorem I.3.2
542	(`extend_to_av`) and Corollary I.1.2 (a `thm:rigidity_lemma`
543	consequence).
544	
545	Blueprint reference: `thm:albanese_universal_property` (Milne,
546	*Abelian Varieties*, Proposition III.6.1, p. 104). -/
547	
548	/-- **Albanese universal property of `Pic⁰_{C/k̄}` — Milne III §6
549	Proposition 6.1.**
550	
551	For a complete nonsingular curve `C` of genus `g > 0` over an
552	algebraically closed field `k̄`, a marked `k̄`-point `P₀ ∈ C(k̄)`, and
553	every pointed morphism `φ : C ⟶ A` into an abelian variety `A` with
554	`φ(P₀) = η_A`, there exists a *unique* regular morphism
555	`ψ : Pic⁰_{C/k̄} ⟶ A` such that `φ = ι_{P₀} ≫ ψ`.
556	
557	Proof sketch (Milne III.6.1):
558	1. **Symmetrisation.** `(P₁,…,P_g) ↦ φ(P₁) + ⋯ + φ(P_g)` is
559	   `S_g`-symmetric (`A` commutative), so factors through
560	   `Sym^g C` as `Sym^g φ` (`lem:symmetric_product_av_map`).
561	2. **Descent to a regular morphism on `J`.** The birational morphism
562	   `f^{(g)} : Sym^g C ⟶ Pic⁰_{C/k̄}` (`lem:symmetric_product_to_jacobian`)
563	   exhibits `Sym^g φ ∘ (f^{(g)})^{-1}` as a rational map
564	   `Pic⁰_{C/k̄} ⇢ A`, which by Milne Theorem I.3.2 extends uniquely to
565	   a regular morphism `ψ : Pic⁰_{C/k̄} ⟶ A`
566	   (`lem:descent_through_birational_sigma`).
567	3. **Factorisation `ψ ∘ ι_{P₀} = φ`.** Use Milne's identification of
568	   `ι_{P₀}` with the composite `Q ↦ Q + (g − 1) P₀` followed by
569	   `f^{(g)}`; together with `φ(P₀) = η_A` and the additive structure
570	   of `A`, this gives `ψ(ι_{P₀}(Q)) = φ(Q)` on `k̄`-points, hence
571	   globally by the reduced-and-separated agreement principle.
572	4. **Homomorphism property.** `ψ` sends `η_J = ι_{P₀}(P₀)` to
573	   `φ(P₀) = η_A`, so by Milne Corollary I.1.2 (a `thm:rigidity_lemma`
574	   consequence) it is a homomorphism of group schemes.
575	5. **Uniqueness.** Two homomorphisms `Pic⁰_{C/k̄} ⟶ A` with the same
576	   restriction to `ι_{P₀}(C)` agree on the `g`-fold sum
577	   `ι_{P₀}(C) + ⋯ + ι_{P₀}(C) = Pic⁰_{C/k̄}` (since `f^{(g)}` is
578	   surjective), hence are equal.
579	
580	The statement asserts only the existence and uniqueness of the factoring
581	morphism `ψ : Pic⁰_{C/k̄} ⟶ A` (matching the project's `IsAlbanese`
582	convention in `Jacobian.lean`); the group-homomorphism property is implicit
583	in the construction, by Milne Corollary I.1.2 (registered in
584	`chap:AbelianVarietyRigidity`).
585	
586	The proof below is pure assembly: `descentThroughBirationalSigma` (§5)
587	transported across `albanese_eq_iff_symmetricPower_eq` (§5.5). Both of
588	those, and the constructions of §1–§4 they rest on, are still unproved —
589	see the file header. -/
590	theorem albanese_universal_property
591	    (_hg : 0 < genus C)
592	    (P0 : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of kbar))) ⟶ C)
593	    {A : Over (Spec (.of kbar))}
594	    [GrpObj A] [IsProper A.hom] [Smooth A.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom]
595	    (φ : C ⟶ A) (_hφ : P0 ≫ φ = η[A]) :
596	    ∃! (ψ : jacobianScheme C ⟶ A), φ = abelJacobi C P0 ≫ ψ := by
597	  -- Transport the symmetric-power descent `descentThroughBirationalSigma`
598	  -- across the connecting biconditional `albanese_eq_iff_symmetricPower_eq`.
599	  have key := albanese_eq_iff_symmetricPower_eq C P0 φ _hφ
600	  obtain ⟨ψ, hψ_sym, huniq_sym⟩ := descentThroughBirationalSigma C P0 φ _hφ
601	  exact ⟨ψ, (key ψ).mpr hψ_sym,
602	    fun ψ' hψ' => huniq_sym ψ' ((key ψ').mp hψ')⟩
603	
604	end Pic0
605	
606	end AlgebraicGeometry
